turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select
the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I screened for: (1) broken inversion symmetry, (2) heavy polarizable anions Te/Se > S > halides, (3) d10 cations Cu+/Ag+/Hg2+/Cd2+ and/or lone-pair cations, and (4) low-symmetry/aligned acentric coordination rather than high-symmetry centrosymmetric rocksalt/zinc-blende/perovskite-like cells.

The strongest SHG candidates are the low-symmetry heavy chalcogenides/tellurides. c073 is triclinic/P1-like and Te/As-rich with Cd/In d10 character, so it should have very large off-diagonal components. c080 combines Hg–Se and Ga–Se acentric units in a low-symmetry cell. c069 has Ag–Te/S mixed-anion acentric packing. c070 is a non-centrosymmetric cubic telluride with Cu/Ta and large d14-type response. c079 is a low-symmetry Ba–Ge–Te/Se structure with mixed heavy chalcogens and no clear inversion center.

Final: c073, c080, c069, c070, c079
